The e-TellTale sensor is a strip with a strain gauge sensor at its base.
The sensor is used to detect flow separation and reattachment dynamics over wind turbine blades.
The Reynolds number based on the chord length of the 2D blade section is 2.105.
The amplitude of the blade oscillation is 5°.
The Γ criterion method is used to identify vortices.
The stall and reattachment instant are defined as tref (ic) = (t +t )/2 and tref (ic) = (t +t )/2, respectively.
The time scale of the separation/detachment phenomena is ∼ 10c/U.
The location of the separation/detachment point is within one third of the blade chord from the leading edge.
The POD analysis is used to characterize the coherent structure organization during the blade oscillation cycle.
The PIV acquisition rate used for the POD analysis is 1600 Hz.
The spatial resolution of the PIV velocity fields is 6.3 px/mm.
The strip detection method is used to extract movements of the e-TellTale strip within the flow field.
The Vortex identification method is used to identify vortices in the shear areas over the blade surface.
The Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is used to detect flow separation and reattachment dynamics.
The e-TellTale sensor is compared to three different post-processing methods.
The results show good agreement between the measured velocity field and movements of the strip regarding the separation/reattachment dynamics.
